title: Generation, maintenance, and monitoring of gnotobiotic mice
protocol: Don a sterile surgical gown and sterile gloves.
Decontaminate BSC to create a sterile working surface following steps 4–8 of before you begin section.
Wash hands with antiseptic soap.
Cover the bottom of a decontaminated biosafety cabinet with a sterile drape, thus creating a sterile work surface.
Delineate a working area for the person handling the sterile materials and a working area for the individual handling non-sterile materials on the sterile drape.
Open the "gavage kit" and place the sterile internal contents on the sterile drape-covered working surface.
Transfer the cultured bacteria into a conical tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 4°C, 3000 g for 10 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the bacterial pellet in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) to the desired concentration/volume for gavage.
Transfer the inoculum into sterile 2 mL tubes using a 2-person technique within the sterile work surface in the BSC.
Hold the tube while an assistant transfers the inoculum with a sterile micropipette tip without touching the tube exterior.
Place the tube(s) containing the prepared inoculum into the "gavage kit".
Seal the gavage kit properly.
Place the bacterial inoculum tube(s) into the "gavage kit" under sterile conditions.
Decontaminate BSC to create a sterile working surface.
Import germ-free animals into the BSC.
Open the gavage kit within the BSC and remove the sterile internal contents.
Attach the gavage needle to the 1 mL syringe.
Draw up 0.2 ml of bacterial inoculum for each mouse.
Restrain the mouse and hold it upright.
Insert the tip of the gavage needle into the stomach of the animal.
Administer the bacterial inoculum.
Return the mouse to the sterile isocage.
Monitor germ-free and gnotobiotic conditions in mice using bacterial culture, microscopy with Gram staining or nuclear DNA staining, and 16S rRNA gene amplification and sequencing.
Decontaminate a BCS and create a sterile work surface.
Open autoclaved 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes onto the sterile work surface.
Don a sterile surgical gown and sterile gloves.
Import isocages containing gnotobiotic mice into decontaminated BSC.
Collect fecal samples from each mouse under sterile conditions.
Place collected fecal samples in appropriate number of microcentrifuge tubes per animal.
Transport microcentrifuge tubes containing fecal samples to the laboratory for further analysis.
Weigh fecal pellets and add sterile PBS at a concentration of 100 mg/mL.
Mix using a vortex mixer for 1 minute until a homogeneous suspension is achieved.
Prepare 10-fold serial dilutions in sterile PBS.
Plate 10 μL of each dilution in triplicate on agar plates.
Incubate under appropriate conditions for the bacterial species or consortium.
Count CFU and express results as CFU/g of feces.
Homogenize feces (3–5 fresh fecal pellets) in 0.3 mL sterile PBS by vortex mixing.
Add 0.15 mL of the homogenate to 0.15 mL 4% paraformaldehyde stock solution.
Mix using a vortex mixer.
Incubate for 45 minutes at room temperature (21°C–25°C).
Prepare a SYTOX Green working solution by adding 1.5 μL of 5 mM SYTOX Green into 0.9 mL PBS.
Add 0.1 mL of the fixed fecal homogenate to the SYTOX Green working solution.
Incubate at room temperature for 1 hour protected from light.
Spread 25 μL on a glass slide and air dry.
Visualize using a fluorescence microscope at 400× to 1000× magnification.
Homogenize feces as described in step 10a.
Add 10 μL of fecal homogenate onto a glass slide.
Air dry the sample.
Fix by quickly exposing the back of the slide over a flame three times.
Immerse the fixed slide in Crystal Violet solution for 1 min.
Immerse the fixed slide in Stabilized Iodine for 1 min.
Wash the slide thoroughly with a mixture of acetone and isopropanol (1:3) until excess Crystal-Violet and Stabilized Iodine are removed and the run-off is clear.
Rinse the slide with distilled water.
Immerse the slide in Safranin solution for 2 min.
Rinse the slide with distilled water and air dry.
Visualize using a bright-field microscope (400–1000× magnification).
Extract genomic DNA from fecal sample using QIAamp PowerFecal Pro DNA Kit following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Amplify the 16S rRNA gene via PCR using specified thermocycling conditions.
Run the PCR products on a 1% agarose gel at 120 V.
Prepare the PCR reaction product for sequencing by cleaning up with QIAGEN’s PCR MinElute Purification kit following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Elute with 10 μL of molecular grade water and measure the final DNA concentration.
Sequence the PCR reaction product using the Sanger method.
Analyze sequence data by alignment using a sequence database (e.g., Nucleotide BLAST).
